stem.text: Express \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{k=1}^{n} 5\sqrt{4 + \frac{3k}{n}} \cdot \frac{3}{n} \) as a definite integral in the variable x, taking x to be the sample point \( 4 + \frac{3k}{n} \).

worked_solution.text: The factor \( \frac{3}{n} \) is the subinterval width, so the interval has length 3.
The sample point is \( 4 + \frac{3k}{n} \), which is 4 plus k widths, so the interval starts at x = 4 and ends at x = 4 + 3 = 7.
worked_solution.rule_named: sample point gives the lower limit

worked_solution.text: The remaining factor is the function evaluated at the sample point, so the limit equals \( \int_{4}^{7} 5\sqrt{x}\,dx \).
worked_solution.rule_named: limit of Riemann sums as a definite integral
